Path.dc.html.title: 4 · The path + who does the work

guide.text:
How to use this blueprint

This canvas is the design for /services. The homepage and the work page have their own canvases; this one covers only the services page.

To change something, name the section and the change, e.g. "In 3 · Engagements, put IT STOPS AT above YOU GET." Edit a section board on the right and the full desktop page follows. The phone board is separate: say so when a change should reach phones too.

The open decision
• Pricing carries no numbers. Nothing here commits to a price or to a free review, because pricing research has not happened yet. When it does, the PRICING band is where it lands.

Where things will live in the code
• Service names, fit, outcome, boundary: the offers list in src/lib/content.ts
• Page copy: a new src/content/services dictionary, same pattern as src/content/work
• Page and sections: src/app/services/page.tsx and src/app/services-v2.css
• Footer and navigation words: src/components/site-shell.tsx

Design rules (same as the homepage and work page)
• Forest #071C18, cream #EEE7DE, sand #E5DBD1, card #F6F1EA, copper #CF8649, copper text #8F5327
• Manrope for headings, Inter for text, square corners except the navigation pill
• 72px side margin on desktop, 20px on phones
• Sections alternate forest and cream so the page has a rhythm rather than one long field

decisions.text:
Decisions in this design

• Three engagements, not four. Product Blueprint, Launch Sprint and Product Care are modes of working — decide, build, keep running. "Operations Platform" was a kind of product sitting in a list of engagement modes, so it moves into "What we build" as an example of what a Launch Sprint produces. This is the one structural change from the current src/lib/content.ts, and it means the work page hero drops from four names to three.

• Two axes, stated separately. What we build (web apps and dashboards, mobile apps, integrations and automation) is a different question from how we work (the three engagements). Mixing them is what made the old list feel arbitrary.

• Every engagement card says where it stops. A boundary is the most useful thing a services page can give a buyer, and the least common.

• Pricing is answered, not dodged, but carries no number. The page says how price is set and what you own, and sends the visitor to a project review.

• The founder is named once, under "Who does the work", because accountability is a fair thing to name. The rest of the page says "we".

• The closing asks for a project review, matching the work page, so both pages land on the same next step.

Motion
• Hero: eyebrow, headline and lead rise in; a warm light drifts behind
• The path thread draws itself left to right once
• Engagement cards lift slightly on hover
• Everything stops under reduce-motion
